claim: Engineering references only; none is asserted as a normative product standard for the GraphX fixture waveform.

references.title: Multipath propagation and parameterization of its characteristics
references.adaptation: The harness represents a channel as a normalized linear transversal filter of delayed complex replicas and reports tap power, mean delay, RMS delay spread, and Doppler separately. No ITU environment distribution or qualification limit is imported.

references.title: Study on channel model for frequencies from 0.5 to 100 GHz
references.adaptation: Only the TDL vocabulary—relative delays, normalized tap powers, fading coefficients, and Doppler—is used. GraphX uses small explicit engineering tap sets, not a claimed 3GPP deployment scenario.

references.title: Wideband transmission systems; Data transmission equipment operating in the 2,4 GHz band; Harmonised Standard for access to radio spectrum
sections: 5.4.11 Receiver Blocking test conditions and method
references.adaptation: The published method motivates recording wanted level, blocker frequency/level, communication performance, and each tested combination. The GraphX harness adapts this only to calibrated complex-baseband engineering SIR sweeps; it does not reproduce the 2.4 GHz bands, receiver categories, dBm limits, companion-device procedure, conducted/radiated setup, or any regulatory conformance claim.

references.title: Jakes fading model revisited
sections: sum-of-sinusoids Rayleigh fading construction and second-order behavior
references.adaptation: The implemented time-varying engineering Rayleigh option is a reproducible finite sum of complex sinusoids with component frequencies bounded by the declared maximum Doppler. Analytical tests cover component support, finite-record power, and autocorrelation. It is not labeled as an exact standardized Jakes deployment profile, and composite instantaneous phase is not bounded near fading nulls.
